module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 936

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/936](https://www.erdosproblems.com/936)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Nat

namespace Erdos936

/--
The predicate that `a n` is only powerful for finitely many `n`.
-/
def EventuallyNotPowerful (a : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop := atTop.Eventually (fun n => ¬ (a n).Powerful)

/-- Is $2^n + 1$ powerful for finitely many $n$? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_936.variants.two_pow_add_one :
   answer(sorry) ↔ EventuallyNotPowerful (2 ^ · + 1) := by
  sorry

/-- Is $2^n - 1$ powerful for finitely many $n$? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_936.variants.two_pow_sub_one :
   answer(sorry) ↔ EventuallyNotPowerful (2 ^ · - 1) := by
  sorry

/-- Is $n! + 1$ powerful for finitely many $n$? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_936.variants.factorial_add_one :
   answer(sorry) ↔ EventuallyNotPowerful (·! + 1) := by
  sorry

/-- Is $n! - 1$ powerful for finitely many $n$? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_936.variants.factorial_sub_one :
   answer(sorry) ↔ EventuallyNotPowerful (·! - 1) := by
  sorry

end Erdos936

reformulations.difference: All four variants express finiteness of the powerful indices using eventual non-powerfulness atTop on ℕ, rather than an explicitly finite set of indices.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: On ℕ, atTop equals the cofinite filter. Consequently, EventuallyNotPowerful a ↔ {n : ℕ | (a n).Powerful}.Finite. This equivalence and its invariance under discarding any finite initial interval were proved in the scratch file. Although Nat.Powerful includes zero, the minus sequences attain zero only at finitely many initial indices, so the convention cannot change any of the four questions.

review.notes: Checked the helper and all four theorem statements against the official source, including its remarks. No mathematical mismatches found. The latest retrieved official snapshot marks the problem open and mentions only abc-conditional results; the current independent Erdős database also records it as open. The live source returned a Cloudflare challenge, so archived copies were used. Lean checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean verified the prime-square characterization of Powerful, finiteness equivalences, boundary examples, and agreement of natural subtraction with integer subtraction. The equivalence proofs do not depend on sorry-backed declarations.
